articles.title: Sets of codimension larger than the dimension are empty
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a subset of an
extended metric space and let $n < c$ be natural numbers. If $S$ has Hausdorff codimension at
least $c$ in dimension $n$, then $S$ is empty.

articles.title: The empty set has every codimension
articles.statement:
In an extended metric space, the empty set has
Hausdorff codimension at least $c$ in dimension $n$ for all natural numbers $n$ and $c$.

articles.title: Characterization of Hausdorff codimension
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a subset of an extended metric
space and let $n, c$ be natural numbers. Then $S$ has Hausdorff codimension at least $c$ in
dimension $n$ if and only if either $S$ is empty, or both $c \le n$ and the Hausdorff
dimension of $S$ satisfies $\dim_H S \le n - c$.

articles.title: A dimension bound gives a codimension bound
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a subset of an extended metric
space and let $c \le n$ be natural numbers. If the Hausdorff dimension of $S$ satisfies
$\dim_H S \le n - c$, then $S$ has Hausdorff codimension at least $c$ in dimension $n$.

articles.title: Lower bound on Hausdorff codimension
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a subset of an extended metric space
and let $n, c$ be natural numbers. The set $S$ has Hausdorff codimension at least $c$ in
dimension $n$ if $S$ is empty or its Hausdorff dimension satisfies $\dim_H S + c \le n$, the
inequality being taken in $[0, \infty]$.

The empty-set case plays the role of the convention $\dim_H \emptyset = -\infty$.

articles.title: Subsets inherit a codimension bound
articles.statement:
Let $T \subseteq S$ be subsets of an extended
metric space and let $n, c$ be natural numbers. If $S$ has Hausdorff codimension at least $c$
in dimension $n$, then so does $T$.

articles.title: Affine-symmetric iterated function system
articles.statement:
Let $(f_i)_{i < n}$ be a finite family of maps
$f_i \colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ on Euclidean space. The family is affine-symmetric with
common contraction factor $\lambda$ if $0 < \lambda < 1$ and there are linear isometries
$A_i \colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ (orthogonal transformations) and vectors
$\beta_i \in \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $f_i(x) = \lambda A_i(x) + \beta_i$ for every $i < n$ and every
$x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

articles.title: Attractor of an iterated function system
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space and let
$(f_i)_{i < n}$ be a finite family of maps $X \to X$. A set $S \subseteq X$ is an attractor of the
family if it is nonempty and compact and is fixed by the Hutchinson operator, that is,
$S = \bigcup_{i < n} f_i(S)$.

articles.title: Moran's equality for affine-symmetric iterated function systems
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let
$(f_i)_{i < n}$ be an affine-symmetric iterated function system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with common
contraction factor $\lambda \in (0,1)$ that satisfies the open set condition. Then every attractor
$S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of the system has Hausdorff dimension

$$\dim_H S = -\frac{\log n}{\log \lambda}.$$

## Sources

- P. A. P. Moran, *Additive functions of intervals and Hausdorff measure*, Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 42 (1946); J. E. Hutchinson, *Fractals and self similarity*, Indiana Univ. Math. J. 30 (1981). Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §105. Problem `moran_equality_affine` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Open set condition
articles.statement:
A finite family of maps $f_i \colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$,
$i < n$, satisfies the open set condition if there is a nonempty open set $G \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$
such that $f_i(G) \subseteq G$ for every $i < n$ and the images $f_i(G)$ and $f_j(G)$ are disjoint
whenever $i \neq j$.

articles.title: Continuous cutoff for a closed-embedding homomorphism
articles.statement:
A continuous nonnegative compactly supported cutoff normalized on every
left orbit meeting `K`, for a closed-embedding homomorphism `ι`. The measure
may have any scale. No Hausdorff or countability hypotheses are required.

articles.title: Continuous Bruhat cutoff for a closed subgroup
articles.statement:
A continuous nonnegative compactly supported Bruhat cutoff for a closed
subgroup, normalized on any subset of the saturation of a compact set.

articles.title: Existence of a Bruhat section for a closed subgroup
articles.statement:
A Bruhat section: given a closed subgroup `T` of a locally compact group
and a set `E` contained in `T * C` for compact `C`, there is a compactly
supported nonnegative measurable function `w` whose integral over each
`T`-translate meeting `E` equals `1`.

Use `exists_continuous_cutoff_of_subset_mul` when continuity or boundedness is
needed. These functions normalize subgroup integrals; they are not sections
of the quotient map.

articles.title: Existence of a locally constant normalized subgroup cutoff
articles.statement:
A compact set in a topological group with a compact open subgroup has a
nonnegative locally constant cutoff whose integral over every left
`T`-orbit meeting that set is one, for a closed commutative subgroup `T`.
The same compactly supported function works simultaneously on all of
`T * Ω`. The Haar measure need not have any prescribed normalization.

articles.title: Positive common integral of cocompact subgroup cutoffs
articles.statement:
A compact cocompactness witness gives a continuous normalized cutoff and
a positive common integral for all nonnegative measurable compactly supported
normalized cutoffs. Every such cutoff is genuinely integrable, even when it
is not bounded. Neither the ambient group nor the subgroup must be Hausdorff.

articles.title: Integrability is independent of the orbit-normalized weight
articles.statement:
Integrability of an invariant complex function times a nonnegative real
weight is independent of the weight when both orbit averages are one on the
function's support. Neither weighted function is required to be integrable.

articles.title: Bounded invariant functions are integrable against normalized cutoffs
articles.statement:
A bounded measurable `T`-invariant complex function is integrable against
any nonnegative measurable compactly supported weight whose `T`-average is
one wherever the function is nonzero. The weight need not be bounded.

articles.title: Cutoff independence of integrals of bounded invariant functions
articles.statement:
The integral of a bounded measurable `T`-invariant complex function
against a nonnegative measurable compactly supported cutoff does not depend
on the cutoff, when each cutoff has subgroup integral one on the support of
that function. Normalization is not required outside its support.

The more general `integral_mul_eq_of_normalized_subgroup` does not require
boundedness or compact support; the hypotheses here also guarantee
integrability by `integrable_mul_of_integral_subgroup_translate_eq_one`.

articles.title: Orbit-normalized cutoffs give equal complex integrals
articles.statement:
Weighted integrals of an invariant complex function agree for nonnegative
orbit-normalized cutoffs. If one weighted function is not integrable, neither
is the other, and both Bochner integrals are zero.

articles.title: Subgroup-normalized weights give equal integrals
articles.statement:
Subgroup-normalized nonnegative weights give the same integral of an
invariant complex function. This measure-theoretic statement requires neither
a closed subgroup nor compact supports nor a bounded function.

articles.title: Orbit-normalized weights give equal nonnegative integrals
articles.statement:
Nonnegative integrals of an invariant function agree for orbit-normalized
weights. Normalization is needed only where the function is nonzero, and the
common integral is allowed to be infinite.

articles.title: Measurable fundamental domains for discrete subgroups
articles.statement:
Every discrete subgroup of a second-countable Hausdorff topological group
admits a measurable fundamental domain for the opposite action, simultaneously
for every measure.

articles.title: Fundamental domain for a subgroup of countable index
articles.statement:
From a fundamental domain for `Γ₁`, a countable union of inverse
coset-representative translates gives a fundamental domain for a subgroup
`Γ₂ ≤ Γ₁` of countable index.

articles.title: Integrals over a subgroup fundamental domain as sums over cosets
articles.statement:
If `𝓕` is a fundamental domain for `Γ₁` and `R` is a system of
representatives for the left cosets of `Γ₂` in `Γ₁`, then integrals over
the union of the translates `((R i)⁻¹) • 𝓕` unfold into sums over `i` of
integrals over `𝓕`, for both `ℝ≥0∞`-valued and Bochner integrals.

articles.title: Right-invariant Haar measures are inversion-invariant
articles.statement: A right-invariant Haar measure is invariant under inversion.

articles.title: Haar measures on GL(2, F) are right- and inversion-invariant
articles.statement: Every Haar measure on `GL (2, F)` is right-invariant and inversion-invariant.

articles.title: GL(2, F) is unimodular
articles.statement: The modular character of `GL (2, F)` is trivial: `GL (2, F)` is unimodular.

articles.title: Decay of dilates of an integrable function
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be
Lebesgue integrable and let $\lambda > 0$. Then for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$,
$n^{-\lambda} f(nx) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ through the positive integers.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_37`.

articles.title: Unbounded multipliers preserving almost-everywhere convergence to zero
articles.statement:
Let
$(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of Borel measurable functions $f_n : \mathbb{R} \to
\mathbb{R}$ such that $f_n(x) \to 0$ for almost every $x \in [0, 1]$. Then there is a sequence of
real numbers $(c_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $|c_n| \to \infty$ such that $c_n f_n(x) \to 0$ for
almost every $x \in [0, 1]$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_38`.

articles.title: The standard simple approximations converge uniformly where the function is bounded
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space and $f : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ a measurable function. Let
$r_0, r_1, \ldots$ be the fixed enumeration of $\mathbb{Q}$ by natural-number codes ($r_k = 0$ when
$k$ codes no rational), put $q_k = \max(r_k, 0)$, and let
$\varphi_n(a) = \max(\{0\} \cup \{q_k : k < n,\ q_k \le f(a)\})$ be the $n$-th standard simple
approximation of $f$. Then for every $B \in [0, \infty)$ and every $\varepsilon \in (0, \infty]$
there is $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $f(a) - \varphi_n(a) < \varepsilon$ for all $n \ge N$ and
all $a \in \alpha$ with $f(a) \le B$, where subtraction in $[0, \infty]$ is truncated at $0$.

articles.title: Approximation of nonnegative measurable functions by simple functions
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a
measurable space and $f : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ a measurable function. There is a sequence of
simple functions $\varphi_n : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$) such that:
(a) $\varphi_0 \le \varphi_1 \le \cdots \le f$ pointwise; (b) $\varphi_n(a) \to f(a)$ for every
$a \in \alpha$; and (c) for every $B \in [0, \infty)$ and every $\varepsilon \in (0, \infty]$ there
is $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $f(a) - \varphi_n(a) < \varepsilon$ for all $n \ge N$ and all
$a \in \alpha$ with $f(a) \le B$, where the subtraction in $[0, \infty]$ is truncated at $0$.

articles.title: Bounded convergence theorem, $L^1$ form
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a measurable
space $\alpha$, let $G$ be a real normed space, let $C$ be a real number, and let
$F_n : \alpha \to G$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $f : \alpha \to G$ be functions. Suppose that each
$F_n$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable, that for every $n$ we have $\|F_n(a)\| \le C$ for
$\mu$-almost every $a$, and that $F_n \to f$ in $\mu$-measure. Then
$\int_\alpha \|F_n(a) - f(a)\| \, d\mu(a) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Bounded convergence theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$,
let $G$ be a real normed space, let $C$ be a real number, and let $F_n : \alpha \to G$ for
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $f : \alpha \to G$ be functions. Suppose that each $F_n$ is almost
everywhere strongly measurable, that for every $n$ we have $\|F_n(a)\| \le C$ for $\mu$-almost
every $a$, and that $F_n \to f$ in $\mu$-measure (in probability). Then
$\int_\alpha F_n \, d\mu \to \int_\alpha f \, d\mu$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: The $L^0$ pseudometric on $(0,1)$
articles.statement:
For Borel measurable functions
$f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$,

$$
d(f,g) = \int_{[0,1]} \frac{|f(x) - g(x)|}{1 + |f(x) - g(x)|}\,dx,
$$

the integral being with respect to Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$.

This is a pseudometric: functions that agree almost everywhere on $[0,1]$ are at distance $0$,
and on the almost-everywhere classes it is the usual metric of $L^0([0,1])$.

articles.title: Measurable functions representing $L^0((0,1))$
articles.statement:
The type of Borel measurable functions
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, used as representatives of the elements of $L^0([0,1])$.

The pseudometric and the convergence in measure built on them depend only on the restriction
of $f$ to $[0,1]$ up to a null set.

articles.title: Convergence in the $L^0$ pseudometric is convergence in measure
articles.statement:
Let $f$ and
$f_0, f_1, f_2, \ldots$ be Borel measurable functions $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, and let $d$ be
the pseudometric

$$
d(g,h) = \int_{[0,1]} \frac{|g(x) - h(x)|}{1 + |g(x) - h(x)|}\,dx
$$

on such functions, the integral being with respect to Lebesgue measure. Then
$d(f_n, f) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ if and only if $f_n \to f$ in measure with respect to
Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, the Lebesgue measure of
$\{x \in [0,1] : |f_n(x) - f(x)| \ge \varepsilon\}$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.

The source states this for $L^0([0,1])$, on which $d$ is a metric; here it is stated for
representatives, on which $d$ is only a pseudometric. Both sides depend only on the
almost-everywhere classes of the functions on $[0,1]$, so the two statements say the same thing.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_07`, with the change above.

articles.title: Integrability of the convolution integrand
articles.statement:
Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let
$f, g : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be Lebesgue integrable. Identify $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$ with
$\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d$ by writing a point as $(x, y)$, where $x$ consists of its first
$d$ coordinates and $y$ of its last $d$ coordinates. Then the function
$(x, y) \mapsto f(x - y)\, g(y)$ is Lebesgue integrable on $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_72`.

articles.title: Exponential kernel approximate identity
articles.statement:
For every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$
in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} n\int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x)f(y)e^{-2n|x-y|}\,dy\,dx
= \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x)^2\,dx,
$$

where $n$ runs through the natural numbers and the integrals are with respect to Lebesgue measure.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_96`.

articles.title: Convolution of an integrable and a bounded function is uniformly continuous
articles.statement:
Let
$d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be Lebesgue integrable, and let
$g : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be Borel measurable and bounded. Then the convolution

$$
(f * g)(x) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(x - y)\, g(y)\, dy
$$

is uniformly continuous on $\mathbb{R}^d$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_15`.

articles.title: Smoothness of compactly supported parameter integrals
articles.statement:
The integral `p ↦ ∫ x, w x • Ψ (c x, p) ∂μ` of a smooth compactly
supported function is smooth in the parameter `p`.

articles.title: Differentiating an integral of a series term by term
articles.statement:
Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\Omega$
be an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$, let $a < c < b$ be real numbers, and for each
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $f_n : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be almost everywhere
measurable on $\Omega \times (a, b)$ with respect to Lebesgue measure. Write
$\partial_y f_n(x, y)$ for the derivative of $t \mapsto f_n(x, t)$ at $y$, taken to be $0$ where
this derivative does not exist, and give every series that does not converge absolutely the
sum $0$. Assume that:
(1) for each $n$ and almost every $x \in \Omega$, the function $y \mapsto f_n(x, y)$ is
absolutely continuous on $[a, b]$;
(2) each $\partial_y f_n$ is almost everywhere measurable on $\Omega \times (a, b)$, the series
$\sum_n |\partial_y f_n(x, y)|$ converges for almost every $(x, y) \in \Omega \times (a, b)$,
and its sum is integrable on $\Omega \times (a, b)$;
(3) the series $\sum_n |f_n(x, c)|$ converges for almost every $x \in \Omega$, and its sum is
integrable on $\Omega$.
Then there is a function $F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that for almost every
$y \in (a, b)$ the function $x \mapsto \sum_n f_n(x, y)$ is integrable on $\Omega$,
$F(y) = \int_\Omega \sum_n f_n(x, y)\, dx$, and $F$ is differentiable at $y$ with

$$
F'(y) = \sum_n \int_\Omega \partial_y f_n(x, y)\, dx.
$$

The joint measurability of each $f_n$ is a hypothesis of the source that the first formalization
dropped. It is needed: for $d \ge 1$ and nonempty bounded $\Omega$, a non-measurable $f_0$ of
modulus one that does not depend on $y$, with $f_n = 0$ for $n \ge 1$, satisfies the other
hypotheses but not the conclusion.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_50`, with the change above.

articles.title: Egorov's theorem on the real line under integrable domination
articles.statement:
Let
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be any function and let $f_n : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$,
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, be Borel measurable functions with $f_n(x) \to f(x)$ for almost every
$x \in \mathbb{R}$. Let $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be Lebesgue integrable with
$|f_n(x)| \le g(x)$ for all $n$ and all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there
is a Borel set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ of Lebesgue measure less than $\varepsilon$ such that
$f_n \to f$ uniformly on $\mathbb{R} \setminus E$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_43`.

articles.title: Upper bound for the integral of the logarithm of a probability density over a set
articles.statement:
Let
$\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $X$ and let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable with
respect to $\mu$, with $f(x) > 0$ for every $x \in X$ and $\int_X f\,d\mu = 1$. Then for every
measurable set $E \subseteq X$ with $0 < \mu(E) < \infty$ such that $\log f$ is integrable on $E$,

$$
\int_E \log f\,d\mu \le \mu(E)\log\frac{1}{\mu(E)}.
$$

The integrability of $\log f$ on $E$ is assumed so that the statement is real-valued: the
positive part of $\log f$ is integrable on $E$ (since $(\log f)^{+}\le f$), so if $\log f$
is not integrable on $E$ then $\int_E(\log f)\,d\mu=-\infty$ and the inequality holds in
$\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_82`.

articles.title: Two-sided bound for the integral of the square root of one plus a square
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a
probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$ and let $h : \Omega \to [0,\infty)$ be a
measurable function with $\int_\Omega h\,d\mu < \infty$. If $A = \int_\Omega h\,d\mu$, then

$$
\sqrt{1+A^2}\le \int_\Omega \sqrt{1+h^2}\,d\mu \le 1+A.
$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_66`.

articles.title: Lusin's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological space with its Borel
$\sigma$-algebra, and let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $X$ that is regular: finite on compact
sets, outer regular, and inner regular on open sets by compact sets. Let $Y$ be a
second-countable topological space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and let $f : X \to Y$ be
measurable. Then for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a compact set $K \subseteq X$ with
$\mu(X \setminus K) < \varepsilon$ such that $f$ is continuous on $K$.

## Sources

- G. B. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Lusin's theorem.

articles.title: Tonelli for products
articles.statement:
Let $\mu_i$ be σ-finite measures on measurable spaces $X_i$,
indexed by a finite type $\iota$, and let $g_i : X_i \to [0, \infty]$ be measurable functions.
Then the integral of $y \mapsto \prod_{i \in \iota} g_i(y_i)$ with respect to the product measure
$\prod_i \mu_i$ equals $\prod_{i \in \iota} \int g_i \, d\mu_i$.

articles.title: Iterated integrals of a product of one-variable functions
articles.statement:
Let $\mu_i$ be σ-finite
measures on measurable spaces $X_i$, indexed by a finite type $\iota$, and let
$g_i : X_i \to [0, \infty]$ be measurable functions. For a finite set $s \subseteq \iota$ and a
point $x \in \prod_i X_i$, integrating $y \mapsto \prod_{i \in \iota} g_i(y_i)$ over the
coordinates $y_i$ with $i \in s$, each against $\mu_i$, while the other coordinates are fixed to
those of $x$, gives $\left(\prod_{i \in s} \int g_i \, d\mu_i\right) \cdot
\prod_{i \notin s} g_i(x_i)$.

articles.title: A product of measures with densities
articles.statement:
Let $\mu_i$ be σ-finite measures on measurable
spaces $X_i$, indexed by a finite type $\iota$, and let $f_i : X_i \to [0, \infty]$ be measurable
functions such that, for each $i$, the measure $f_i \mu_i$ with density $f_i$ with respect to
$\mu_i$ is σ-finite. Then the product measure $\prod_i f_i \mu_i$ equals the measure with density
$y \mapsto \prod_{i \in \iota} f_i(y_i)$ with respect to the product measure $\prod_i \mu_i$.

The σ-finiteness of the weighted measures guarantees that their product measure is characterized
on boxes.

articles.title: Scheffé's lemma
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let
$f_n : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$) be $\mu$-almost everywhere strongly measurable,
and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be in $L^1(\mu)$. Write
$\|h\|_1 = \int |h| \, d\mu \in [0, \infty]$ for the $L^1$ seminorm. If $f_n(x) \to g(x)$ for
$\mu$-almost every $x$ and $\|f_n\|_1 \to \|g\|_1$ in $[0, \infty]$, then $\|f_n - g\|_1 \to 0$,
that is, $f_n \to g$ in $L^1(\mu)$.

articles.title: Scheffé's lemma for convergence in measure
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space
$\alpha$, let $f_n : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$) and $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
in $L^1(\mu)$, and write $\|h\|_1 = \int |h| \, d\mu$. If $f_n \to g$ in $\mu$-measure (for every
$\varepsilon > 0$, $\mu\{x : |f_n(x) - g(x)| \ge \varepsilon\} \to 0$) and $\|f_n\|_1 \to \|g\|_1$,
then $\|f_n - g\|_1 \to 0$, that is, $f_n \to g$ in $L^1(\mu)$.

The proof applies Scheffé's lemma along a further subsequence, extracted from every subsequence by
convergence in measure.

articles.title: Scheffé's lemma on the real line
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable and
let $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of integrable real functions $f_n$ on $\mathbb{R}$
such that $f_n(x) \to f(x)$ for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$. If
$\int_{\mathbb{R}} |f_n| \to \int_{\mathbb{R}} |f|$ as $n \to \infty$, then
$\int_{\mathbb{R}} |f_n - f| \to 0$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_76`.

articles.title: Convergence in measure with converging L¹ norms implies uniform integrability
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$
be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $f_n : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$)
and $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be in $L^1(\mu)$, and write $\|h\|_1 = \int |h| \, d\mu$. If
$f_n \to g$ in $\mu$-measure (for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
$\mu\{x : |f_n(x) - g(x)| \ge \varepsilon\} \to 0$) and $\|f_n\|_1 \to \|g\|_1$, then the family
$(f_n)$ is uniformly integrable: $\sup_n \|f_n\|_1 < \infty$, and the supremum of
$\int_s |f_n| \, d\mu$ over all $n$ and all sets $s \subseteq \alpha$ with $\mu(s) \le \delta$
tends to $0$ as $\delta \to 0$.

The proof combines the $L^1$ convergence $\|f_n - g\|_1 \to 0$ given by Scheffé's lemma for
convergence in measure with the Vitali convergence theorem.

articles.title: Uniform integrability equivalences
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a measurable space
$\alpha$, let $f_n : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$) and $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
in $L^1(\mu)$, write $\|h\|_1 = \int |h| \, d\mu$, and suppose that $f_n \to g$ in $\mu$-measure
(for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $\mu\{x : |f_n(x) - g(x)| \ge \varepsilon\} \to 0$). Then the
following are equivalent: (1) the family $(f_n)$ is uniformly integrable, that is,
$\sup_n \|f_n\|_1 < \infty$ and the supremum of $\int_s |f_n| \, d\mu$ over all $n$ and all sets
$s \subseteq \alpha$ with $\mu(s) \le \delta$ tends to $0$ as $\delta \to 0$; (2) $f_n \to g$ in
$L^1(\mu)$, that is, $\|f_n - g\|_1 \to 0$; (3) $\|f_n\|_1 \to \|g\|_1$.

The equivalence of (1) and (2) is the Vitali convergence theorem; (3) implies (2) by Scheffé's
lemma for convergence in measure, and (2) implies (3) by the reverse triangle inequality.

articles.title: Sets of positive measure contain three-term arithmetic progressions
articles.statement:
For every Borel set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ of positive Lebesgue measure there exist $x \in A$ and $y > 0$ such that
$x + y \in A$ and $x - y \in A$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_75`.

articles.title: Sets of finite Lebesgue measure contain no right half-line
articles.statement:
Let $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
have finite Lebesgue outer measure ($E$ need not be measurable). Then for every real $X$ there
is a real $x > X$ with $x \notin E$; that is, $E$ contains no half-line $(X, \infty)$.

articles.title: The graph of a measurable function is a null set
articles.statement:
Let $d \ge 0$ be an integer and let
$f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be Borel measurable. Identify $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}$
with $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ by taking the last coordinate as $y$. Then the graph
$\Gamma = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R} : y = f(x)\}$ is a Borel measurable subset
of $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ and has Lebesgue measure $0$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_38`.

articles.title: Sets with locally null image have null image
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a second-countable topological
space, $Y$ a measurable space with a measure $\mu$, $f : X \to Y$ a function and $s \subseteq X$.
If every point $x \in s$ has a neighbourhood $V$ with $\mu(f(V \cap s)) = 0$, then
$\mu(f(s)) = 0$.

Here $\mu$ is evaluated as an outer measure, so the images need not be measurable.

articles.title: Nonzero polynomials over nondiscrete fields have Haar-null zero sets
articles.statement:
A nonzero multivariate polynomial over a nondiscrete locally compact
second-countable Hausdorff topological field has an additive Haar-null zero set.
This includes the empty variable type.

articles.title: Determinant formula for the area of a triangle
articles.statement:
Write $x = (x_1, x_2)$ for the
coordinates of a point $x$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. For all points $a, b, c$ in
$\mathbb{R}^2$, the Lebesgue measure (area) of the convex hull of $\{a, b, c\}$, as a real
number, equals $\frac{1}{2}\,\lvert (b_1 - a_1)(c_2 - a_2) - (b_2 - a_2)(c_1 - a_1) \rvert$.

articles.title: Volume of the cross-polytope
articles.statement:
For every integer $n \ge 1$, the cross-polytope
$\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : |x_1| + \dots + |x_n| \le 1\}$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ has
volume $2^n / n!$.

## Sources

- optimizationproblems `constants/25a.md`, line 44 (the polar-volume identity).

articles.title: Volume of the coordinate cube
articles.statement:
For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate cube
$[-1, 1]^n$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ has volume $2^n$.

## Sources

- optimizationproblems `constants/25a.md`, line 44 (the cube-volume identity).

articles.title: Area of the unit square
articles.statement:
The closed unit square
$\{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : 0 \le x_1 \le 1 \text{ and } 0 \le x_2 \le 1\}$ in the Euclidean plane has
Lebesgue measure (area) $1$.

articles.title: $L^p$ functions whose integrals over $(0, L)$ tend to $0$ form a Borel set
articles.statement:
Let
$1 \le p \le \infty$. The set of real-valued $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R})$ (with respect to Lebesgue
measure) such that $\int_0^L f(x)\,dx \to 0$ as $L \to +\infty$ is a Borel subset of
$L^p(\mathbb{R})$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Set functions, measures and integrals with values in abstract spaces), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_25`.

articles.title: Functions with vanishing integrals over $(0, L)$
articles.statement:
For $0 \le p \le \infty$, this is the set
of real-valued $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R})$ (with respect to Lebesgue measure) such that
$\int_{[0, L]} f(x)\,dx \to 0$ as $L \to +\infty$, where the integral of a function that is not
integrable on $[0, L]$ counts as $0$.

articles.title: Partitions of the unit interval
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, real numbers
$t_0, t_1, \dots, t_n$ form a partition of $[0, 1]$ when $0 = t_0 < t_1 < \dots < t_n = 1$.

articles.title: Lebesgue integrals over truncations of a set
articles.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be Lebesgue measure on
$\mathbb{R}$, let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be measurable, and let $g : \mathbb{R} \to [0, \infty]$
be measurable. Then

$$\int_S g \, d\lambda = \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \int_{[-n, n] \cap S} g \, d\lambda.$$

This is monotone convergence applied to the indicators of the truncations.

articles.title: $L^p$ on $(0,1)$ via averages over partitions
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be in
$L^1([0, 1])$ and let $p > 1$ be a real number. Then $f \in L^p([0, 1])$ if and only if there is
a real number $C$ such that

$$\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (t_{i+1} - t_i)
\left(\frac{1}{t_{i+1} - t_i} \int_{t_i}^{t_{i+1}} |f(x)|\,dx\right)^p \le C$$

for every partition $0 = t_0 < t_1 < \dots < t_n = 1$ of $[0, 1]$. Here $L^1([0, 1])$ and
$L^p([0, 1])$ are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to $[0, 1]$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_02`.

articles.title: Characterization of $L^p$ membership via truncated integrals
articles.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be Lebesgue
measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let $F$ be a second-countable normed additive commutative group with its
Borel $\sigma$-algebra, let $0 < p < \infty$, let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be measurable, and let
$f : \mathbb{R} \to F$ be measurable. Then $f$ belongs to $L^p$ of $\lambda$ restricted to $S$ if
and only if

$$\sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \int_{[-n, n] \cap S} \|f(x)\|^p \, d\lambda(x) < \infty,$$

where the integrals are taken in $[0, \infty]$.

articles.title: Polynomial decay implies $L^p$ membership
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed additive commutative group
and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be almost everywhere strongly measurable. Suppose there are real
numbers $C \ge 0$ and $q > 1$ such that $\|f(x)\| \le C (1 + |x|)^{-q}$ for almost every
$x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R})$, with respect to Lebesgue measure, for every
$p \in [1, \infty]$.

articles.title: Pointwise polynomial decay implies $L^p$ membership
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a normed additive
commutative group and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be almost everywhere strongly measurable. Suppose
there are real numbers $C \ge 0$ and $q > 1$ such that $\|f(x)\| \le C (1 + |x|)^{-q}$ for every
$x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R})$, with respect to Lebesgue measure, for every
$p \in [1, \infty]$.

articles.title: Partition average sum
articles.statement:
For a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, a real number $p$
and real numbers $t_0, t_1, \dots, t_n$, the partition average sum is

$$\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (t_{i+1} - t_i)
\left(\frac{1}{t_{i+1} - t_i} \int_{[t_i, t_{i+1}]} |f(x)|\,dx\right)^p,$$

where the integrals are Lebesgue integrals over the closed intervals $[t_i, t_{i+1}]$ (empty when
$t_{i+1} < t_i$), the integral of a function that is not integrable there counts as $0$, $1/0 = 0$,
and $0^p$ is taken to be $1$ when $p = 0$ and $0$ when $p \ne 0$.

articles.title: Continuity of the cutoff approximants
articles.statement:
Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a real
normed space and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be continuous. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$
the $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ is continuous.

articles.title: Cutoff approximants vanish at the left endpoint
articles.statement:
Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a
real normed space and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be any function. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
the $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ takes the value $0$ at $a$.

articles.title: Cutoff approximants vanish at the right endpoint
articles.statement:
Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a
real normed space and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be any function. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
the $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ takes the value $0$ at $b$.

articles.title: Cutoff approximants stay in $L^p$
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a real normed space, let $\mu$ be a measure
on $\mathbb{R}$, let $p \in [0, \infty]$, and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be continuous with
$g_0 \in L^p(\mu)$. Then for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th cutoff
approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ lies in $L^p(\mu)$.

The approximant is pointwise dominated by $\|g_0\|$, since the cutoff factor takes values in
$[0, 1]$.

articles.title: Cutoff approximants
articles.statement:
Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a real normed space, let
$g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and put $\delta_n = (b - a)/(n + 1)$. The $n$-th
cutoff approximant of $g_0$ with endpoints $a$ and $b$ is the function
$x \mapsto \varphi(x)\, g_0(x)$, where $\varphi$ is the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$,
$b$ and width $\delta_n$.

articles.title: Continuous functions vanishing at the endpoints are dense in $L^p$ of a compact interval
articles.statement:
Let $a < b$ be real numbers, let $1 \le p < \infty$ and let $E$ be a real normed space. Write
$L^p([a, b])$ for $L^p$ with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to $[a, b]$. For every
$f : \mathbb{R} \to E$ in $L^p([a, b])$ and every $\varepsilon \in (0, \infty]$, there is a
continuous $g : \mathbb{R} \to E$ with $g(a) = g(b) = 0$, $g \in L^p([a, b])$ and
$\|f - g\|_{L^p([a, b])} < \varepsilon$.

articles.title: Pointwise bound on the cutoff error
articles.statement:
Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, let $E$ be a real normed
space and let $g_0 : \mathbb{R} \to E$. If $g_n$ denotes the $n$-th cutoff approximant of $g_0$
with endpoints $a$ and $b$, then $\|g_0(x) - g_n(x)\| \le \|g_0(x)\|$ for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Continuity of the vanishing cutoff factor
articles.statement:
For all $a, b, \delta \in \mathbb{R}$, the
vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ is a continuous function
$\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: The vanishing cutoff factor equals one on its plateau
articles.statement:
Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and
$\delta > 0$. For every real $x$ with $a + \delta \le x \le b - \delta$, the vanishing cutoff
factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ takes the value $1$ at $x$.

articles.title: The vanishing cutoff factor vanishes at the left endpoint
articles.statement:
For all
$a, b, \delta \in \mathbb{R}$, the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width
$\delta$ takes the value $0$ at $a$.

articles.title: The vanishing cutoff factor vanishes at the right endpoint
articles.statement:
For all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $\delta$, the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$
and width $\delta$ takes the value $0$ at $b$.

articles.title: The vanishing cutoff factor is at most one
articles.statement:
For all real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$
and $x$, the value at $x$ of the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width
$\delta$ is at most $1$.

articles.title: The vanishing cutoff factor is nonnegative
articles.statement:
For all real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$
and $x$, the value at $x$ of the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width
$\delta$ is at least $0$.

articles.title: Vanishing cutoff factor
articles.statement:
For real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$, the value at $x$
of the vanishing cutoff factor with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ is
$\max\bigl(0, \min\bigl(1, \min((x - a)/\delta, (b - x)/\delta)\bigr)\bigr)$, where division
by $0$ is read as $0$.

It vanishes at $a$ and at $b$. For $\delta > 0$ it equals $1$ on $[a + \delta, b - \delta]$,
an interval that is nonempty when $2\delta \le b - a$. At $\delta = 0$ it is identically
zero.

articles.title: Essential supremum of a continuous map
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a compact topological space with
its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, let $\mu$ be a measure on $\alpha$ that is positive on every nonempty
open set, let $E$ be a seminormed additive commutative group, and let $f : \alpha \to E$ be
continuous. Then the essential supremum of $\|f\|$ with respect to $\mu$ equals the supremum norm
$\sup_{x \in \alpha} \|f(x)\|$ of $f$, as an equality in $[0, \infty]$.

articles.title: The $L^\infty$ norm of a continuous map is its supremum norm
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a compact
topological space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, let $\mu$ be a measure on $\alpha$ that is
positive on every nonempty open set, let $E$ be a seminormed additive commutative group such that
$\alpha$ or $E$ is second-countable, and let $f : \alpha \to E$ be continuous. Then
$\|f\|_{L^\infty(\mu)} = \sup_{x \in \alpha} \|f(x)\|$, as an equality in $[0, \infty]$.

articles.title: Uniform $L^p$ bounds on $(0,1)$ give the same $L^\infty$ bound
articles.statement:
Let $M$ be a real number,
write $M^+ = \max(M, 0)$, and let $f_0, f_1, f_2, \dots : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be functions
that are almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to
$[0,1]$. If $\|f_n\|_{L^p[0,1]} \le M^+$ for every $n$ and every real $p \ge 1$, then
$\|f_n\|_{L^\infty[0,1]} \le M^+$ for every $n$. All norms are taken with respect to Lebesgue
measure restricted to $[0,1]$ and may be infinite.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_52`.

articles.title: The $L^p$ norm tends to the $L^\infty$ norm
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a measurable
space $\alpha$ and let $f \colon \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be essentially bounded,
$f \in L^\infty(\mu)$. Then $\|f\|_{L^p(\mu)} \to \|f\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}$ as the real exponent
$p$ tends to $\infty$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_42`.

articles.title: An $L^p$ function with finite $L^q$ mass on finite-measure sets is in $L^q$
articles.statement:
Let
$1 \le p < q < \infty$ and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ belong to $L^p(\mathbb{R})$. If
$\int_A |f|^q < \infty$ for every Borel set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ of finite Lebesgue measure,
then $f \in L^q(\mathbb{R})$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_24`.

articles.title: A bounded integrable function is square integrable
articles.statement:
Let $d$ be a natural number, let
$M \ge 0$, and let $f \colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $|f(x)| \le M$ for every
$x \in \mathbb{R}^d$. If $f \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, then $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and

$$\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)} \le M^{1/2} \, \|f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}^{1/2},$$

where the spaces and norms are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_41`.

articles.title: $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ are incomparable
articles.statement:
Let $d \ge 1$. With respect
to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$, there is a function $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ in
$L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that is not in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, and there is a function
$g : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that is not in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_97`.

articles.title: An integral inequality for $p$-th powers with $0 < p < 1$
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a
measurable space and let $0 < p < 1$. Then for all real-valued $f, g \in L^p(\mu)$,

$$\int \bigl||f|^p - |g|^p\bigr|\,d\mu \le \int |f - g|^p\,d\mu.$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Functional analysis; Linear function spaces and their duals), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_53`.

articles.title: Uniformly large level sets under a reverse Hölder bound
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be Lebesgue measure
on $[0,1]$, and let $f_0, f_1, f_2, \ldots : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ lie in $L^2(\mu)$ with
$\|f_n\|_{L^2(\mu)} \le 2024\,\|f_n\|_{L^1(\mu)}$ for every $n$ and
$\|f_n\|_{L^1(\mu)} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Then there is a sequence of real numbers
$y_n \to \infty$ such that

$$
\inf_n \mu(\{x : |f_n(x)| \ge y_n\}) > 0.
$$

The divergence hypothesis is the limit $\|f_n\|_{L^1(\mu)} \to \infty$ in $[0,\infty]$; the
formal source instead required $\|f_n\|_{L^1(\mu)} = \infty$ for all large $n$, which no function
in $L^2(\mu)$ satisfies, so its statement was vacuous.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_04`, with the change above.

articles.title: Lebesgue measure on the unit interval
articles.statement:
The measure on $\mathbb{R}$ that assigns to each
set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ the Lebesgue measure of $A \cap [0,1]$.

articles.title: Weak $L^p$ limits of nonnegative functions are nonnegative
articles.statement:
Let $1 < p < \infty$
and write $L^p([0,1])$ for the Lebesgue space of real functions on $[0,1]$ with Lebesgue measure.
Let $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $L^p([0,1])$ such that for each $n$,
$f_n(x) \ge 0$ for almost every $x \in [0,1]$, and let $f \in L^p([0,1])$. If $f_n$ converges
weakly to $f$, that is, $\ell(f_n) \to \ell(f)$ for every continuous linear functional
$\ell : L^p([0,1]) \to \mathbb{R}$, then $f(x) \ge 0$ for almost every $x \in [0,1]$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Normed linear spaces and Banach spaces; Banach lattices), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_16`.

articles.title: Lebesgue measure on $(0,1)$
articles.statement:
The measure on $\mathbb{R}$ obtained by restricting
Lebesgue measure to the open interval $(0, 1)$.

articles.title: Bounded almost everywhere convergent sequences in $L^p$, $1 < p < \infty$, converge weakly
articles.statement:
**Bounded almost everywhere convergent sequences in $L^p$, $1 < p < \infty$, converge
weakly.** Let $1 < p < \infty$ and let $q$ be the conjugate exponent, $1/p + 1/q = 1$. Let $f$
and $f_0, f_1, f_2, \dots$ be real-valued functions in $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ such that $f_n \to f$
almost everywhere and $\sup_n \|f_n\|_{L^p} < \infty$. Then $f_n$ converges weakly to $f$: for
every $g \in L^q(\mathbb{R})$,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f_n g\,dx=\int_{\mathbb{R}} f g\,dx.
$$

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Normed linear spaces and Banach spaces; Banach lattices), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_82`.

articles.title: Bounded a.e.-null sequences in $L^p(0,1)$ converge weakly to zero
articles.statement:
Let $1 < p < \infty$
and let $q$ be the conjugate exponent, so that $1/p + 1/q = 1$. Write $L^p(0,1)$ and $L^q(0,1)$
for the Lebesgue spaces of real functions on $(0,1)$ with Lebesgue measure. Let
$(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $L^p(0,1)$ with $\|f_n\|_{L^p} \le 1$ for every $n$
and $f_n(x) \to 0$ for almost every $x \in (0,1)$. Then for every $g \in L^q(0,1)$,

$$
\int_0^1 f_n(x)\, g(x)\, dx \to 0 \quad (n \to \infty).
$$

Since $L^q(0,1)$ is the dual of $L^p(0,1)$, this says that $(f_n)$ converges weakly to $0$ in
$L^p(0,1)$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Functional analysis; Normed linear spaces and Banach spaces; Banach lattices), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_10`.

articles.title: Sierpiński's theorem on atomless measures
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a finite atomless measure. For
every measurable set $s$ and every $t \in [0, \infty]$ with $t \le \mu(s)$, there is a measurable
set $u \subseteq s$ with $\mu(u) = t$.

articles.title: Restriction of an atomless measure
articles.statement:
The restriction of an atomless measure to a
measurable set is atomless.

articles.title: Atomless measure
articles.statement:
A measure $\mu$ on a measurable space is atomless when every
measurable set $s$ with $\mu(s) > 0$ contains a measurable subset $t \subseteq s$ with
$0 < \mu(t) < \mu(s)$.

articles.title: Banach–Tarski paradox for the closed unit ball
articles.statement:
In three-dimensional Euclidean space
$\mathbb{R}^3$, write $\bar B(c, r)$ for the closed ball of radius $r$ about $c$. There are points
$c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R}^3$ such that $\bar B(c_1, 1)$ and $\bar B(c_2, 1)$ are disjoint and the
closed unit ball $\bar B(0, 1)$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with
$\bar B(c_1, 1) \cup \bar B(c_2, 1)$.

## Sources

- S. Banach and A. Tarski, Fund. Math. 6 (1924) 244–277 original paradox; S. Wagon, The Banach–Tarski Paradox, Cambridge Univ. Press (1993); Lean states closed unit ball duplication specialization in ℝ³ with ambient `≃ᵢ` equidecomposability.

articles.title: Equidecomposability via piecewise-isometric bijections
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of a
metric space $X$. Then $A$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B$ if and only if
there are a map $f : X \to X$ and a finite set $S$ of isometric bijections of $X$ onto itself
such that $f$ restricts to a bijection from $A$ onto $B$ and for every $x \in A$ there is
$g \in S$ with $f(x) = g(x)$.

articles.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries
articles.statement:
Let $X$ be a metric space. Subsets $A$ and $B$
of $X$ are finitely equidecomposable by isometries if there are a natural number $n$, sets
$A_1, \dots, A_n$ and $B_1, \dots, B_n$ in $X$, and isometric bijections $g_1, \dots, g_n$ of
$X$ onto itself such that the sets $A_i$ are pairwise disjoint, the sets $B_i$ are pairwise
disjoint, $A = A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_n$, $B = B_1 \cup \dots \cup B_n$, and $g_i(A_i) = B_i$
for every $i$.

articles.title: Equidecomposability of a set with its isometric image
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be an isometric bijection
of a metric space $X$ onto itself. Then every subset $A$ of $X$ is finitely equidecomposable by
isometries with its image $g(A)$.

articles.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries is reflexive
articles.statement:
Every subset $A$ of a metric
space $X$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with itself.

articles.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries is symmetric
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of a
metric space $X$. If $A$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B$, then $B$ is
finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $A$.

articles.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries is transitive
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be subsets
of a metric space $X$. If $A$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B$ and $B$ is
finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $C$, then $A$ is finitely equidecomposable by
isometries with $C$.

articles.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries respects disjoint unions
articles.statement:
Let $A_1$, $A_2$,
$B_1$ and $B_2$ be subsets of a metric space $X$ with $A_1 \cap A_2 = \emptyset$ and
$B_1 \cap B_2 = \emptyset$. If $A_1$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B_1$ and
$A_2$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B_2$, then $A_1 \cup A_2$ is finitely
equidecomposable by isometries with $B_1 \cup B_2$.

articles.title: Carathéodory extension theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an algebra of sets on $\alpha$ and
let $\mu_0$ be an additive content on $\mathcal{A}$ with values in $[0, \infty]$ that is
$\sigma$-subadditive: whenever $s_0, s_1, \dots \in \mathcal{A}$ and
$\bigcup_i s_i \in \mathcal{A}$, we have $\mu_0(\bigcup_i s_i) \le \sum_i \mu_0(s_i)$. Suppose
there are sets $B_0, B_1, \dots \in \mathcal{A}$ with $\bigcup_i B_i = \alpha$ and
$\mu_0(B_i) < \infty$ for every $i$. Then there is exactly one measure $\mu$ on the
$\sigma$-algebra $\sigma(\mathcal{A})$ generated by $\mathcal{A}$ such that
$\mu(s) = \mu_0(s)$ for every $s \in \mathcal{A}$.

articles.title: Existence of the Carathéodory extension
articles.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an algebra of sets on
$\alpha$ and let $\mu_0$ be an additive content on $\mathcal{A}$ with values in $[0, \infty]$
that is $\sigma$-subadditive: whenever $s_0, s_1, \dots \in \mathcal{A}$ and
$\bigcup_i s_i \in \mathcal{A}$, we have $\mu_0(\bigcup_i s_i) \le \sum_i \mu_0(s_i)$. Then there
is a measure $\mu$ on the $\sigma$-algebra $\sigma(\mathcal{A})$ generated by $\mathcal{A}$ such
that $\mu(s) = \mu_0(s)$ for every $s \in \mathcal{A}$.

articles.title: Every algebra of sets is a π-system
articles.statement:
If $\mathcal{A}$ is an algebra of sets on $\alpha$,
then $\mathcal{A}$ is a $\pi$-system: for all $s, t \in \mathcal{A}$ with $s \cap t$ nonempty, we
have $s \cap t \in \mathcal{A}$.

articles.title: Every algebra of sets is a semiring of sets
articles.statement:
If $\mathcal{A}$ is an algebra of sets on
$\alpha$, then $\mathcal{A}$ is a semiring of sets: $\emptyset \in \mathcal{A}$, $s \cap t \in
\mathcal{A}$ for all $s, t \in \mathcal{A}$, and for all $s, t \in \mathcal{A}$ the difference
$s \setminus t$ is the union of finitely many pairwise disjoint members of $\mathcal{A}$.

articles.title: Congruent plane sets
articles.statement:
Two sets $E$ and $F$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ are
congruent when some isometry of the plane onto itself maps $E$ onto $F$.

articles.title: Problem of a congruence-invariant countably additive plane measure
articles.statement:
The countably additive reading of Problem 169: there is a function
`μ`, defined for all plane sets, equal on congruent sets, countably
additive, extending the Caratheodory linear measure (read as Lebesgue
volume on measurable sets), with values in `[0, +∞]` (automatic for
`ENNReal`).

articles.title: Congruence-invariant set functions on the plane
articles.statement:
A function $\mu$ that assigns to every
subset of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ a value in $[0, \infty]$ is congruence invariant when
$\mu(E) = \mu(F)$ for all congruent plane sets $E$ and $F$.

articles.title: Countably additive set function
articles.statement:
`μ` is countably additive on pairwise-disjoint families. This is the
countably-additive reading of "additive" in Problem 169; the typescript
does not say whether finite or countable additivity is meant.

articles.title: No countably additive congruence-invariant measure on all plane sets
articles.statement:
The countably additive reading is false in ZFC. Sketch: let
`V₀ ⊆ [0,1]` meet each `ℚ`-coset of `ℝ` exactly once (Vitali selector)
and put `V = V₀ × [0,1]`. Enumerating `ℚ ∩ [-1,1]` as `(qₙ)`, the
translates `Tₙ = V + (qₙ, 0)` are pairwise disjoint, each congruent to
`V`, so all have the same mass `c = μ V`. Their union contains the unit
square `Q = [0,1] × [0,1]` and lies in the strip `[-1,2] × [0,1]` of
volume 3, so countable additivity and monotonicity give
`1 = μ Q ≤ μ U ≤ 3`, while countable additivity also gives
`μ U = ∑'ₙ c`, which is `0` if `c = 0` and `+∞` if `c > 0`, a
contradiction. Hence no such `μ` exists. This refutes the countably
additive formalization only. The typescript says bare "additive"; the
finite-additivity reading is Banach's 1923 theorem (a Banach measure: a
finitely additive, isometry-invariant function on all plane sets
extending Lebesgue measure), not this claim, and is not asserted here.

## Sources

- E. Szpilrajn, Problem 169 of the Scottish Book; typescript PDF p.78, printed p.75. Banach, Fund. Math. 4 (1923), 7-33.

articles.title: Base of a measure
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $X$. A class $B$ of
subsets of $X$ is a base of $\mu$ if every set in $B$ is measurable, $B$ is stochastically
independent with respect to $\mu$, and every measurable set $A \subseteq X$ agrees up to a null
set with a set $C$ in the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $B$, that is, $\mu(A \triangle C) = 0$.

articles.title: Convex measure
articles.statement:
A measure $\mu$ on a measurable space $X$ is convex (in Fréchet's sense,
"sans singularités") if $\mu(X) = 1$ and every measurable set $A$ with $\mu(A) > 0$ contains a
measurable subset $B$ with $0 < \mu(B) < \mu(A)$.

articles.title: Stochastically independent class of sets
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space
$X$. A class $B$ of subsets of $X$ is stochastically independent with respect to $\mu$ if for
every finite collection of distinct sets $A_1, \dots, A_n$ in $B$, including the empty one,
$\mu(A_1 \cap \dots \cap A_n) = \mu(A_1) \cdots \mu(A_n)$. The empty intersection is $X$ and the
empty product is $1$, so this forces $\mu(X) = 1$. The sets in $B$ need not be measurable; on
such sets $\mu$ is the outer measure.

articles.title: The claim of Szpilrajn's Problem 191
articles.statement:
The proposition, Szpilrajn's Problem 191 from the
Scottish Book in its original form, that for every measurable space $X$, every convex measure
$\mu$ on $X$ has a base, that is, some class $B$ of subsets of $X$ is a base of $\mu$.

articles.title: Szpilrajn's Problem 191 has a negative answer
articles.statement:
The claim of Szpilrajn's Problem 191 is false:
not every convex measure possesses a base. That is, there are a measurable space $X$ and a convex
measure $\mu$ on $X$ such that no class of subsets of $X$ is a base of $\mu$.

A non-atomic (convex) measure has a base if and only if its
measure algebra is homogeneous, and the direct sum of Lebesgue measure
spaces gives a counterexample whose measure algebra is not homogeneous.

## Sources

- E. Szpilrajn, Problem 191 of the Scottish Book; the sets `B n` of numbers in `[0, 1]` whose `n`-th binary digit is `1` form a base for Lebesgue measure on `[0, 1]`. See the commentary in R. D. Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2015).

articles.title: Lyapunov convexity theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a finite atomless measure on a measurable space
$\alpha$, let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, and let $f : \alpha \to E$ be Bochner
integrable with respect to $\mu$. Then the Lyapunov range of $f$ with respect to $\mu$, the set of
integrals $\int_s f \, d\mu$ over measurable sets $s \subseteq \alpha$, is compact and convex.

## Sources

- A. Lyapunov, Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR 4 (1940) 465–478; Diestel-Uhl, Vector Measures; Lean states atomless finite measure case with Bochner integrable finite-dim integrand, infinite-dim fails.

articles.title: Lyapunov range
articles.statement:
For a measure $\mu$ on a measurable space $\alpha$ and a function
$f : \alpha \to E$ into a real normed space $E$, the Lyapunov range of $f$ with respect to $\mu$ is
the set $\lbrace \int_s f \, d\mu : s \subseteq \alpha \text{ measurable} \rbrace$ of integrals of
$f$ over measurable subsets of $\alpha$.

Here $\int_s f \, d\mu$ is the Bochner integral, which is $0$ when $f$ is not integrable on $s$
or when $E$ is not complete.

articles.title: Von Neumann measures on a complete Boolean algebra
articles.statement:
A real-valued function $\mu$ on a
complete Boolean algebra $B$ is a measure in von Neumann's sense when $\mu(\bot) = 0$,
$\mu(a) > 0$ for every $a \ne \bot$, and $\mu$ is countably additive: for every sequence
$(a_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of pairwise disjoint elements of $B$ (that is, $a_i \wedge a_j = \bot$
whenever $i \ne j$), the series $\sum_i \mu(a_i)$ converges and
$\mu(\bigvee_i a_i) = \sum_i \mu(a_i)$.

Von Neumann's conditions (1)-(4) are the axioms of a complete Boolean algebra.

articles.title: The countable chain condition for complete Boolean algebras
articles.statement:
A complete Boolean algebra
$B$ satisfies the countable chain condition (von Neumann's condition (5)) when every subset
$S \subseteq B$ whose distinct elements are pairwise disjoint (that is, $a \wedge b = \bot$ for
all distinct $a, b \in S$) is at most countable.

articles.title: Von Neumann's generalized distributivity law
articles.statement:
A complete Boolean algebra $B$ satisfies
the generalized distributivity law (von Neumann's condition (6)) when, for every double sequence
$(a_{i,j})_{i, j \in \mathbb{N}}$ of elements of $B$ that is increasing in $j$ for each fixed $i$
(that is, $a_{i,0} \le a_{i,1} \le \cdots$ for every $i$),

$$\bigwedge_{i} \bigvee_{j} a_{i,j} = \bigvee_{f} \bigwedge_{i} a_{i,f(i)},$$

where $f$ ranges over all functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Von Neumann's conditions do not guarantee a measure
articles.statement:
There is a complete Boolean algebra that
satisfies the countable chain condition and the generalized distributivity law but carries no
measure in von Neumann's sense; that is, von Neumann's sufficiency claim is false. This answers
Problem 163 of the Scottish Book in the negative, in its stated form.

The typescript's complement clause prints its two constants swapped relative to its own usage
elsewhere; it is read here as the standard complement laws, with bottom $\bot$ and top $\top$.

## Sources

- J. von Neumann, Problem 163 of the Scottish Book; refuted by M. Talagrand, "Maharam's problem", arXiv:math/0601689 (2006), who constructed an exhaustive submeasure not equivalent to a measure, solving the problems of J. von Neumann (1937) and D. Maharam (1947).

articles.title: Von Neumann's sufficiency claim
articles.statement:
The statement that every complete Boolean algebra
satisfying the countable chain condition and the generalized distributivity law carries a
measure in von Neumann's sense.

articles.title: Szpilrajn's Problem 170: plane sets with measurable homeomorphic copies
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a subset
of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every subset $T$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ homeomorphic to $S$ (as
a subspace) is Lebesgue measurable, that is, Carathéodory measurable with respect to Lebesgue
outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. Then $S$ is absolutely measurable: for every measure $\mu$ on
the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb{R}^2$, the set $S$ is Carathéodory measurable with respect
to the outer measure induced by $\mu$.

The hypothesis concerns every subset of the plane homeomorphic to $S$, not only the images of $S$
under homeomorphisms of the whole plane.

## Sources

- E. Szpilrajn, Problem 170 of the Scottish Book; the affirmative answer follows from an unpublished result of J. von Neumann, as recorded in Ad 170 of the typescript. See the commentary in R. D. Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2015). Lebesgue measurability is stated as Carathéodory measurability with respect to `volume`; the case of linear sets, and the analogue for generalized homeomorphisms in the sense of Kuratowski, were already known.

articles.title: Nonempty bounded half-open intervals
articles.statement:
The family of all intervals
$(l, u] \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ with real endpoints $l < u$. It is used as a generating π-system for
the Borel σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Rectangle uniqueness for measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$
articles.statement:
Let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be finite
measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. If $\mu_1((a, b]) = \mu_2((a, b])$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with
$a_i \le b_i$ for every $i$, where $(a, b] = \prod_{i=1}^d (a_i, b_i]$, then $\mu_1 = \mu_2$.

The finiteness hypothesis is essential: for $d \ge 1$, counting measure and twice counting measure
agree on every rectangle (both give $\infty$ on every nonempty rectangle and $0$ on every empty
one) but are distinct.

articles.title: Uniqueness from rectangle values
articles.statement:
Let $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$, and let $\mu_1$
and $\mu_2$ be measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Suppose that for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with
$a_i \le b_i$ for every $i$, both $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ assign the rectangle
$(a, b] = \prod_{i=1}^d (a_i, b_i]$ the mass $\max(\Delta_{a,b} F, 0)$, where $\Delta_{a,b} F$
is the rectangle value of $F$ at $a, b$. Then $\mu_1 = \mu_2$.

This is the uniqueness half of the characterization of measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ by a
distribution function. No finiteness hypothesis is needed: the rectangle formula itself forces
the measures to be finite on every rectangle $(a, b]$.

articles.title: Quadrant uniqueness for measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be finite measures
on $\mathbb{R}^d$. If $\mu(\{x : x \le a\}) = \nu(\{x : x \le a\})$ for every $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$,
where $x \le a$ means $x_i \le a_i$ for every $i$, then $\mu = \nu$.

This is the multivariate analogue of a CDF determining a probability measure.

articles.title: Half-open intervals generate the Borel σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}$
articles.statement:
The Borel σ-algebra on
$\mathbb{R}$ is the σ-algebra generated by the nonempty bounded half-open intervals $(l, u]$
with $l < u$.

articles.title: Lower orthants generate the product σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}^d$
articles.statement:
The product σ-algebra on
$\mathbb{R}^d$, built from the Borel σ-algebra on each coordinate, is generated by the boxes
$\prod_{i=1}^d (-\infty, a_i]$ for $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

articles.title: Half-open intervals countably span $\mathbb{R}$
articles.statement:
There is a sequence of nonempty bounded
half-open intervals $(l, u]$ with $l < u$ whose union is $\mathbb{R}$; for example, the intervals
$(-n - 1, n + 1]$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Nonempty bounded half-open intervals form a π-system
articles.statement:
If two intervals $(l, u]$ and
$(l', u']$ in $\mathbb{R}$ with $l < u$ and $l' < u'$ intersect, then their intersection is again
an interval $(l'', u'']$ with $l'' < u''$.

articles.title: Lower orthants form a π-system
articles.statement:
For $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$ let
$L_a = \prod_{i=1}^d (-\infty, a_i]$. If two such boxes $L_a$ and $L_b$ intersect, then their
intersection is $L_c$ for some $c \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

articles.title: Rectangle value of a function
articles.statement:
For $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ and arbitrary
$a, b \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the rectangle value of $F$ at $a, b$ is

$$\Delta_{a,b} F = \sum_{S \subseteq \{1, \dots, d\}} (-1)^{|S|} F(v_S),$$

where $v_S \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is the vertex with $(v_S)_i = a_i$ for $i \in S$ and $(v_S)_i = b_i$
for $i \notin S$.

Write $(a, b] = \prod_{i=1}^d (a_i, b_i]$. When $a_i \le b_i$ for every $i$ and $F$ is a
distribution function on $\mathbb{R}^d$, this signed inclusion–exclusion sum equals the mass
$\mu((a, b])$ of the associated measure $\mu$.

articles.title: Vertex of a rectangle
articles.statement:
Let $d$ be a natural number, let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and let
$S$ be a finite set of coordinate indices in $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$. The vertex of the rectangle
$(a, b]$ selected by $S$ is the point $v \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $v_i = a_i$ for $i \in S$ and
$v_i = b_i$ for $i \notin S$.

As $S$ ranges over all $2^d$ subsets of indices, these points are the vertices used in
inclusion-exclusion sums over the rectangle.

articles.title: Vitali's theorem
articles.statement:
There exists a subset of $\mathbb{R}$ that is not Lebesgue measurable.

## Sources

- G. Vitali, Sul problema della misura dei gruppi di punti di una retta, Tipografia Gamberini e Parmeggiani, Bologna (1905). Here `NullMeasurableSet` w.r.t. `volume` is the Lebesgue-measurability notion, i.e. measurability for the completion of Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: Dual feasible pair of potentials
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces and let
$c : X \times Y \to \mathbb{R}$. A pair of functions $\varphi : X \to \mathbb{R}$ and
$\psi : Y \to \mathbb{R}$ is dual feasible for the cost $c$ when $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are
continuous and $\varphi(x) + \psi(y) \le c(x, y)$ for all $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$.

articles.title: Coupling of two probability measures
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability measures on
measurable spaces $X$ and $Y$. A probability measure $\pi$ on $X \times Y$ is a coupling of
$\mu$ and $\nu$ when its marginals are $\mu$ and $\nu$, that is, when the pushforward of $\pi$
under the projection $X \times Y \to X$ is $\mu$ and the pushforward of $\pi$ under the
projection $X \times Y \to Y$ is $\nu$.

articles.title: Kantorovich duality on compact metric spaces
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be nonempty compact metric
spaces, each carrying its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability measures on
$X$ and $Y$, and let $c : X \times Y \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous. Then the infimum of
$\int c \, d\pi$ over all couplings $\pi$ of $\mu$ and $\nu$ equals the supremum of
$\int \varphi \, d\mu + \int \psi \, d\nu$ over all pairs of continuous functions
$\varphi : X \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\psi : Y \to \mathbb{R}$ such that
$\varphi(x) + \psi(y) \le c(x, y)$ for all $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$.

## Sources

- L. V. Kantorovich, On the Translocation of Masses (1942); English transl. J. Math. Sci. 133 (2006), 1381-1382, DOI 10.1007/S10958-006-0049-2; modern ref C. Villani, Topics in Optimal Transportation (2003).

articles.title: Values of the transport cost over couplings
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability measures
on measurable spaces $X$ and $Y$, and let $c : X \times Y \to \mathbb{R}$. The primal values of
$c$ for $\mu$ and $\nu$ form the set of real numbers $\int c \, d\pi$, where $\pi$ ranges over
the couplings of $\mu$ and $\nu$.

Here $\int c \, d\pi$ is the Bochner integral, which is $0$ when $c$ is not $\pi$-integrable.

articles.title: Couplings
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be measurable spaces, $P$ a measure on $X$ and $Q$ a measure
on $Y$. A coupling of $P$ and $Q$ is a probability measure $\pi$ on $X \times Y$ whose marginals
are $P$ and $Q$: the pushforward of $\pi$ under the projection $X \times Y \to X$ is $P$, and its
pushforward under the projection $X \times Y \to Y$ is $Q$. The set of couplings is written
$\Pi(P, Q)$.

articles.title: Kantorovich cost
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be measurable spaces and
$c \colon X \times Y \to [0, \infty]$ a cost function. The Kantorovich cost of a measure $\pi$ on
$X \times Y$ is $I(\pi) = \int_{X \times Y} c \, d\pi \in [0, \infty]$, the Lebesgue integral of
$c$ against $\pi$ (for a non-measurable $c$, the lower Lebesgue integral).

articles.title: Monge–Kantorovich existence theorem
articles.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be Polish spaces with their Borel
$\sigma$-algebras, let $P$ and $Q$ be probability measures on $X$ and $Y$, and let
$c \colon X \times Y \to [0, \infty]$ be continuous. Then there is a coupling $\pi$ of $P$ and $Q$
whose Kantorovich cost $\int c \, d\pi$ is at most the Kantorovich cost $\int c \, d\pi'$ of every
coupling $\pi'$ of $P$ and $Q$: the Kantorovich cost attains its minimum on the set of couplings
of $P$ and $Q$.

## Sources

- L. V. Kantorovich (1942), after G. Monge (1781). Listed as §73 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Problem `monge_kantorovich` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: A $1$-Lipschitz function on $(a,b)$ is absolutely continuous with essentially bounded derivative
articles.statement:
**A $1$-Lipschitz function on $[a,b]$ is absolutely continuous with essentially bounded
derivative.** Let $a \le b$ be real numbers and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy
$|f(x) - f(y)| \le |x - y|$ for all $x, y \in [a, b]$. Then $f$ is absolutely continuous on
$[a, b]$, and its derivative $f'$, taken to be $0$ at points where $f$ is not differentiable, has
finite norm $\|f'\|_{L^\infty[a,b]}$, the essential supremum with respect to Lebesgue measure on
$[a, b]$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Real functions; Functions of one variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_34`.

articles.title: Lipschitz functions are the absolutely continuous functions with bounded derivative
articles.statement:
Let
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $M \ge 0$ be a real number. Then
$|f(x) - f(y)| \le M|x - y|$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ if and only if $f$ is absolutely
continuous on every closed bounded interval and $|f'(x)| \le M$ for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$
(with respect to Lebesgue measure), where $f'(x)$ is taken to be $0$ at points where $f$ is not
differentiable.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Real functions; Functions of one variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_62`.

articles.title: Absolutely continuous functions have the Lusin N property
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to
\mathbb{R}$ be absolutely continuous on every closed bounded interval $[a, b]$. Then $f$ maps
Lebesgue null sets to null sets: for every set $s \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ of Lebesgue outer measure
zero, the image $f(s)$ has Lebesgue outer measure zero.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Real functions; Functions of one variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_75`.

articles.title: Jordan decomposition of a continuous function of bounded variation
articles.statement:
Let
$F : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous and of bounded variation on all of $\mathbb{R}$.
Then there are continuous non-decreasing functions $F_1, F_2 : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such
that $F = F_1 - F_2$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Real functions; Functions of one variable), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_33`.

articles.title: Maximal functions of bounded a.e.-null sequences tend to zero a.e
articles.statement:
Let
$(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $f_n : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, each
Lebesgue measurable on $[0,1]$, such that $f_n(x) \in [0,1]$ for every $n$ and every
$x \in [0,1]$, and $f_n(x) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ for almost every $x \in [0,1]$. For
$x \in [0,1]$ let

$$Mf_n(x) = \sup_I \frac{1}{|I|} \int_I |f_n(y)|\,dy,$$

where the supremum is taken over all closed intervals $I = [a,b]$ with $a < b$ and
$x \in I \subseteq [0,1]$, and $|I| = b - a$. Then $Mf_n(x) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ for almost
every $x \in [0,1]$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_74`.

articles.title: The maximal function of a singular measure is infinite almost everywhere for that measure
articles.statement:
**The maximal function of a singular measure is infinite almost everywhere for that
measure.** Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\mu$ be a Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ that is
mutually singular with respect to Lebesgue measure $m_n$. Write $B(x, r)$ for the open ball of
radius $r$ about $x$ and define $M_\mu : \mathbb{R}^n \to [0, \infty]$ by

$$
M_\mu(x) = \sup_{r>0} \frac{\mu(B(x, r))}{m_n(B(x, r))}.
$$

Then $\mu(\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : M_\mu(x) < \infty\}) = 0$.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level II (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l2_44`.

articles.title: No continuous function agrees a.e. with the indicator of $(0,1)$
articles.statement:
Let $\chi_{[0,1]}$ be
the characteristic function of $[0,1]$. There is no continuous function
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x) = \chi_{[0,1]}(x)$ for almost every
$x \in \mathbb{R}$ with respect to Lebesgue measure.

## Sources

- MA-ProofBench (L. Pu et al., arXiv:2606.13782), Level I (Measure and integration; Classical measure theory), problem `ma_proofbench_l1_28`.
